record.original_question: Can the finite-interval analytical characterization problems for fractional integrals and derivatives be extended from bounded intervals to functions defined on the positive real semi-axis and on the whole real line, while preserving the same notions of admissible fractional integrals, associated fractional derivatives, and desiderata-based operator structure?

evidence.quote: Consider the problems formulated above in the case of the functions defined on the positive real semi-axis and on R.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Background. A fractional integration operator on an interval $I \subseteq \mathbb{R}$ is a one-parameter family $\{I^\alpha\}_{\alpha>0}$ of linear operators acting on a suitable space of functions $f: I \to \mathbb{R}$ that satisfies the following desiderata:

(D1) Interpolation: $I^1 f(x) = \int_a^x f(t)\,dt$ for the natural left endpoint $a$ of $I$ (with $a=0$ when $I = [0,\infty)$ and $a=-\infty$ when $I = \mathbb{R}$).
(D2) Semigroup (index) law: $I^\alpha I^\beta = I^{\alpha+\beta}$ for all $\alpha,\beta > 0$.
(D3) Continuity: $\alpha \mapsto I^\alpha f$ is continuous in an appropriate topology, with $I^\alpha f \to f$ as $\alpha \downarrow 0$.
(D4) Linearity and a suitable form of locality/causality compatible with $I$.

An associated fractional derivative of order $\alpha \in (0,1)$ is an operator $D^\alpha$ that is a left inverse of $I^\alpha$ on an appropriate domain, satisfies $D^\alpha I^\alpha f = f$ and reduces to ordinary differentiation in the limit $\alpha \uparrow 1$.

For $I = [a,b]$ a bounded interval, an analytical characterization is known: under the desiderata (D1)–(D4), the admissible fractional integrals coincide (up to a normalization) with the Riemann–Liouville integrals
$$I^\alpha f(x) = \frac{1}{\Gamma(\alpha)} \int_a^x (x-t)^{\alpha-1} f(t)\,dt,$$
with corresponding fractional derivatives of Riemann–Liouville (or Caputo) type.

Problem. Determine whether the analogous characterization extends to the unbounded settings:

(a) On the positive real semi-axis $I = [0,\infty)$: characterize all one-parameter families $\{I^\alpha\}_{\alpha>0}$ of operators acting on a natural function space on $[0,\infty)$ (e.g., $L^p([0,\infty))$, $C_0([0,\infty))$, or a weighted variant) that satisfy the desiderata (D1)–(D4), and identify the associated fractional derivatives.

(b) On the whole real line $I = \mathbb{R}$: characterize all one-parameter families $\{I^\alpha\}_{\alpha>0}$ on a natural function space on $\mathbb{R}$ satisfying (D1)–(D4) (with the convention that $I^1 f(x) = \int_{-\infty}^x f(t)\,dt$ on functions decaying at $-\infty$), and identify the associated fractional derivatives.

In each case, prove that the family must coincide with the appropriate Liouville-type fractional integral, or exhibit other admissible families.
artifact.status_search_result: The question is posed as an open extension of a finite-interval axiomatic characterization of fractional integrals/derivatives to the half-line and full real line. No definitive published resolution of this specific axiomatic extension was located; the status appears unresolved in the literature consulted.

status_evidence.title: arXiv:2108.04241
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses analytical characterization of fractional integrals and derivatives on finite intervals and raises the extension to the half-line and to R as an open direction.
status_evidence.claim: The extension to unbounded domains is stated as an open question.
